text:
jamie-sales: Heads-up 10: Large broker wants an air-gapped 6-week POC. They asked for a clear ticketing plan, acceptance tests, and model-license boundaries. Need a compact doc we can hand to their procurement/security.

claire-ps: I'll own the ticketing + PS packaging. Quick Q: do we want to create a dedicated JIRA project per POC or use a shared sales-onprem board? They want SLAs on response times for critical hotfixes.

jamie-sales: dedicated ephemeral JIRA is fine for traceability. Keep epic -> install, verify, eval, close. SLA ask: 4hr ack for critical, 24hr ack for high during business hours.

akash-se: Tech constraints: offline install flow must include an immutable manifest `manifest.json` with checksums and SPDX SBOM. We support both SPDX and CycloneDX but prefer SPDX v2.2 for internal tooling. Manifest example: `{
  "images": [{"name":"operator","sha256":"..."}],
  "models": [{"name":"gpt-q-8bit","license":"eval"}]
}`

mara-secops: Security notes: need chain-of-custody for USB deliveries (signed handoff form), attested SBOM, and proof of signature verification steps. Also they require that telemetry is disabled by default and an opt-in periodic export ZIP is the only allowed mechanism.

ben-qa: Acceptance tests I propose (run offline): 1) smoke gen (10 prompts, latency < 300ms p95), 2) embeddings sanity (cosine on known pairs), 3) cold-start inference after restart, 4) rollback validation (apply delta then revert using backup snapshot). Each test should be runnable with a single `run_poc_tests.sh`.

akash-se: Addendum on rollback: our recommended approach is image revert + restore KV cache snapshot. For K8s installs: `kubectl rollout undo deployment/redwood-operator --to-revision=2` + `redwood-restore-kv --from snapshot.tgz`. We'll include exact commands in the runbook.

jamie-sales: Legal/licensing question from buyer: can model weights be used for internal prod after trial?

ryan-legal: Short answer: eval licenses permit evaluation only; production use requires enterprise model license. We can draft a simple addendum that allows conversion to prod license on signature with fee schedule. Also need an IP indemnity clause for customer-supplied models.

mara-secops: They asked about crypto: FIPS 140-2 validated modules for signing and optional AES-GCM hardware offload. If they require FIPS, we must build bundles with FIPS-compliant libs and note that increases packaging lead time by ~3 business days.

claire-ps: PS pricing/discount Q: can we offer a discounted POC kit (packaging + 8 PS hours + runbook)? I can include a line: $X + one-time packaging fee. If they agree to go Dedicated within 30 days, we give a 25% credit back on PS hours.

jamie-sales: Yes to promo, confirm numbers with finance. Also: buyer insists on not storing any customer prompts. Ensure we document ephemeral prompt handling.

akash-se: Implementation note: set data_store.mode=ephemeral in config. Logs that contain prompts are redacted by default; we'll provide a scrub script `redwood-scrub-logs` for their ops to run before any export.

ben-qa: For test data: we should provide a synthetic prompt set (no PII) for acceptance tests. Also include a failure-mode checklist: OOM on quantized runtime, model-mismatch, signature failure, kube node drain.

ryan-legal: Also need their SOC2 contact and proof of encryption-at-rest config. I'll prepare a two-paragraph legal summary for procurement to attach.

deploybot: system: offline bundle v2.4.1 built (sha256: 9f1a...c2d7). Signature detached: v2.4.1.sig.

mara-secops: One more ask: customer demands artifact verification process documented end-to-end including how they can verify signatures offline without depending on our root cert distribution. Suggestion: we provide a verification bundle that contains CA cert + `redwood-verify` binary signed with that CA. They can keep it inside their network.

akash-se: Agreed. We'll produce `verification-kit.tar.gz` containing CA cert, `redwood-verify` binary, checksums.txt, and an example verification script.

claire-ps: Timeline: I can deliver the runbook, verification kit, and sample `run_poc_tests.sh` by EOD tomorrow. Ben will add QA scripts; Akash will add commands and manifest schema; Mara will produce security attestation; Ryan will draft legal summary.

jamie-sales: Solid. I'll assemble a one-page executive summary and the JIRA skeleton, then send to buyer. If we get their signed questionnaire and SCCM contact in 48hrs we can target install kickoff next week.

mara-secops: FYI - one blocker: customer's procurement may insist that Redwood holds signing keys for faster ops. That's enterprise-only. Flag for Jamie to negotiate.

jamie-sales: Will flag. Thanks everyone. :white_check_mark:
